heard: Early spacewalking was so exhausting, it nearly killed astronauts. Pilots suffered extreme overheating without proper foot and body restraints. NASA launched Gemini 12 in November 1966 to solve the problem. Command pilot James Lovell and pilot Buzz Aldrin flew the mission. Aldrin trained for weightlessness inside an underwater neutral buoyancy pool. In orbit, he used custom foot restraints across three spacewalks. His underwater pool training definitively conquered zero gravity physical exhaustion. His techniques proved human beings could safely work outside their spacecraft.
